nm_winter_wall.blurb: Winter Wall is the standout face on Mud Mountain, a limestone sport hill above the town of Truth or Consequences. Nineteen bolted lines run from 5.8 to 5.12, with 5.10 the most common grade and a few each at 5.11 and 5.12, so there is something for a mid-grade climber and a handful of harder projects. The wall looks south and catches sun nearly all day; shade starts to creep across from the left side by mid-afternoon in December, which is why it is a cool-season destination. Anchors are fixed and routes carry grade plaques at the base. The walk in follows cairns along a ridge and up a wash.

nm_new_new_place.blurb: New New Place is a compact basalt cliff on the edge of White Rock, with roughly 18 lines, almost all traditional and one top-rope. Heights reach about 60 to 70 feet. Grades span the 5.6 to 5.12 range, with the heaviest concentration at 5.9 and 5.10 and a few harder lines on top. Climbs tend to have short cruxes broken up by ledges and good rests. The face looks east, so it goes into shade late in the day and is somewhat protected from wind. It sees fewer visitors than the better-known White Rock walls, so you may well have it to yourself. Getting down to the base means a rocky, blocky scramble, a poor fit for dogs or small kids.

nm_08_the_far_side_i.blurb: The Far Side I is one of the numbered walls on the Palomas Peak cliff band in the northern Sandias, above Placitas. It holds about 18 routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a handful of trad cracks, in the 5.8 to 5.13 range; the bulk sit around 5.10 to 5.12. The limestone here is mostly slabs and thin faces with the odd corner and arete, so expect technical footwork, edging and sustained, balancy moves rather than big holds. Walls on the peak run about 50 to 60 feet. The route to the cliff band is a steady uphill hike from the dirt road, roughly half an hour with a full pack.

nm_alcohol_wall.blurb: Alcohol Wall sits at the east end of the Major Wall complex in the Southern Box, near Socorro. It has 18 sport routes on solid rhyolite, with names that all play on drinking. Most of the climbing is 5.10 to 5.11, centered on 5.11, with a few at 5.12 and a single route far harder than the rest; a lone 5.9 is the easy option. Sun stays on the wall until around two in the afternoon, which makes it a good winter choice. A steep trail leads up to the base from the Southern Box parking, passing Major Wall on the way.

nm_main_wall.blurb: Main Wall is the biggest section of Gallows Edge, an east-facing basalt crag in White Rock near Los Alamos known for short, moderate sport lines. It carries about 18 climbs, mostly bolted with a few crack lines and some top-rope options. The grades lean easy: a cluster of 5.4 to 5.8 routes that suit newer leaders, a couple of 5.9s, and one 5.12 for the strong. Because the dark east face soaks up sun it is a good winter pick, and the closely spaced lines can get busy. Several of the bolts and anchors were replaced in a recent rebolting effort.

nm_pogue_s_cave_area.blurb: Near Datil, Pogue's Cave Area is the wall at the left side of the main Enchanted Tower zone, and takes its name from a slot-shaped cave midway across. It is arguably the longest unbroken stretch of climbable wall in the area, with 18 bolted sport routes. The climbing is vertical to overhanging and pocketed, graded from 5.10 to 5.12, with the large majority at 5.11 and only a few each at 5.10 and 5.12, so it rewards climbers working in the low-to-mid 5.11 range. It is popular but usually easy to share. From the road, a short, steep trail of about five minutes leads up to the base.

nm_panorama_wall.blurb: Panorama Wall is an east-facing basalt wall in the Utopian Vistas gorge near Taos, reached by heading south down the drainage from the main cluster of cliffs. It has 18 routes, mostly trad with a few sport lines, and a mix of older and newer climbs. Grades run from 5.9 to 5.12, with 5.10 the biggest group followed by 5.11. The surrounding gorge rock is hard, pocketed volcanic stone, and the area is quiet, with little traffic. Newer routes can have loose holds, so a helmet is a good idea. The gorge is reached on foot from a trailhead along the rim.
